column2: Furusiyya

Riders race to every corner of my realm, from the oases to the city gates, crying that [Root.GetTitledFirstName] holds the Furusiyya. In two months the finest lances, bows and riders of the land will gather to prove who among them is the greatest.
Let them come!

A herald of [From.GetTitledName] rides in, dust on his robes, with a sealed invitation: all who claim skill at arms are called to the Furusiyya, the great contest of riding, archery and war that a sovereign holds but once in a reign. Two months of glory, or of broken bones.
At last!
Pah. Games for children playing at war.

[From.GetTitledName] has called the warriors of the realm to a great Furusiyya. As [From.GetSheHe] is of our house, the people see in it the hard old ways of our blood, and they speak less of our decadence.
A splendid decision!

The tents of the Furusiyya cover the plain outside [Root.Location.GetName]. Lancers on Arabyan chargers, camel riders from the deep desert and archers who can split a reed at a gallop have come at my call. For two months they will show who has the skill of a warrior and who only boasts of it.
A time for heroic deeds.
Alas, the war needs every one of them. Send them home.
You may hold another Furusiyya later
Word comes from [From.GetTitledName]: with the realm at war, the Furusiyya is called off.
Then my blade may yet see real use.
Death closes in, and among my last thoughts is the Furusiyya I called. The games will end with me, and the warriors will have to find another field on which to prove their worth.
May those I ruled remember me for my wisdom.

Peace be upon you, [Root.GetTitledFirstName].\n\n[From.GetTitledFirstName] is dead, and the Furusiyya [From.GetSheHe] called has died with [From.GetHerHim]. The tents are struck and the guests are sent home.
But I was going to prove myself!

My opponent's scimitar slid past my guard and into my belly. As I fell on my back in the sand, I thought for a moment how unfair it all was. Then I listened to my heartbeat fade as the blue sky above me turned darker and darker...
Why me?
My horse shied wildly as my opponent thundered past on his camel, and I was thrown to the hard ground. When my senses returned, my arm was bent at an angle no arm should bend...
A pox on that camel-riding dog!

I sat across a chessboard from my opponent, weighing my opening, when the game beside ours turned violent. One player hurled the board aside and drew his scimitar, and the pieces flew everywhere. A bishop struck me in the eye, and the scimitar did the rest before the guards could part us.
By the Prophet, that is an illegal move!
Master, your honoured guest [From.GetTitledName] has fallen in the games of the Furusiyya.
May [From.GetSheHe] find peace in the life hereafter.
Tell me of the heroes, not the failures!
Master, your honoured guest [From.GetTitledName] has been maimed in the games of the Furusiyya.
May [From.GetSheHe] recover swiftly, [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] willing.
Master, your honoured guest [From.GetTitledName] has taken grave wounds in the games of the Furusiyya.
To my great shame, my bowels gave way in the middle of the melee. I fled the grounds to escape the jeers of my fellow warriors, and to find a change of clothes.
I should have stayed in bed this morning.

In the middle of a wild melee the crowd parted, and there stood a giant of a swordsman, grinning at me. He twirled his blade through a few showy passes and the crowd turned to see what I would do. I put a dagger in his throat. He dropped, and the crowd roared.
Who is next?
Many doubted that I could fight at all. But when we rode out to the mock battle and were ambushed, it was I who rallied our riders and led us to victory against the odds.
I am tougher than I look.
As we rode out to yet another mock battle, I laid a clever ambush in a dry riverbed. We won, though we were outnumbered.
Many more victories will follow.
Many hold chess to be the truest test of a general, and if so my brilliance cannot be denied. Everyone bold enough to sit across the board from me has been beaten.
Checkmate.
I am known for my skill at planning a battle, but a string of foolish blunders in the mock battles has people wondering whether I deserve that name.
I should have seen through that feint...
No matter how hard I try, I cannot get my head around this cursed game of chess. My opponents always seem to be several moves ahead of me.
It is a game for children and weaklings!
After I fell off my horse again and again in the riding contests, many now doubt that I am a warrior at all.
Curse this saddle!
I did not wrestle myself, but I found myself drawn again and again to the wrestling bouts of the Furusiyya, to the oiled, straining bodies of the men...
Such fine, strong men...
While the others busied themselves with feats of arms, I took up other challenges in the many tents that have sprung up outside the grounds. Like the fighters, I came away with sores of my own...
A red badge of courage.
My failures in the contests seem much smaller after a generous cup of wine. The priests frown on it, but surely a few more drops will do no harm...
*hic*

A fighter dared to insult me in front of the other warriors. When I challenged him to a duel his face showed him for the coward he was, but honour left him no choice. I showed no mercy when I cut him down.
All quarrels should be settled thus.

Waiting my turn at the archery butts, I came upon two nomad warriors of the deep desert plotting revenge on a young noble who had called them sand rabble. I watched them cut the girth of his saddle just far enough that it would snap in the coming riding contest.
Clever.

Waiting my turn at the archery butts, I came upon two nomad warriors of the deep desert plotting revenge on a young noble who had called them sand rabble. I told them to face the man openly instead of scheming behind his back like cowards!
No more of this skulking!

Learned men from every corner of the land have come to watch the Furusiyya and trade their wisdom. Between bouts at the wrestling ring I sat with them, and I learned much about how best to rule a land.
I will use this knowledge.
Learned men from every corner of the land have come to watch the Furusiyya and trade their wisdom. I joined one of their debates and gave my own views on how to govern, and they laughed in my face!
Old fools. What do they know?
Two riders of my wing in the coming mock battle were forever at each other's throats. They would sooner have fought each other than our opponents, so for the sake of our side I settled their quarrel.
They agreed to set their feud aside.
Two riders of my wing in the coming mock battle were forever at each other's throats. I called them out for the squabbling brats they were and told them to settle it with blades.
Sadly both were badly hurt, and our wing paid for it...

Between the bouts a sorcerer of the court unrolls a row of carpets on the sand and speaks a word, and they rise to hang at the height of a man's head, rippling like water. Who among the guests will race them around the minarets of the grounds? The riders of horses and camels look at each other. The carpets have no reins.
I will race! How hard can it be?
My feet stay on the ground, where they belong.
I have come out of the Furusiyya as the finest warrior of the land. I have beaten every challenger, and none could match me with bow, lance or horse.
I have been named second champion of the Furusiyya. Few are those who can match my skill at arms.
I have been named third champion of the Furusiyya. My deeds in the contests have shown that I belong among a small circle of elite warriors.
A momentous day.
Let my enemies quake!
I have fought with honour.
[From.GetTitledName] has been named first champion of my great Furusiyya.
[From.GetTitledName] is a mighty warrior indeed.
[From.GetTitledName] fought well enough to be named second champion of my great Furusiyya.
Let no one deny [From.GetHerHis] skill.
The third champion of my Furusiyya is none other than [From.GetTitledName].
Well fought!
[From.GetTitledName] has been named first champion of a great Furusiyya! As [From.GetSheHe] is of our house, the triumph reflects well on all of us, and the people speak less of our decadence.
Congratulations!
[From.GetTitledName] has been named second champion of a great Furusiyya! As [From.GetSheHe] is of our house, the people think the whole house a little less decadent.
Well deserved!
[From.GetTitledName] has won third place in a great Furusiyya! People now think our whole house slightly less decadent, as [From.GetFirstName] is one of us.
Well done!
The Furusiyya is over. The tents are struck, and the tales of its heroes and of its unlucky ones are already spreading through the bazaars of the land.
An event to remember.
The Furusiyya has ended. I was bested more than once, but I tasted victory more than once too. The promise I show as a warrior cannot be denied.
I will improve.
The Furusiyya has ended, and my skill at arms is no longer idle boasting but proven fact. A handful of warriors were better than me, but the glory I won makes me a hero in the eyes of the people.
My enemies will fear me!
The Furusiyya has ended, and not a moment too soon. My showing left much to be desired, and I would have fared worse if some of my opponents had not pitied me.
I did my best...

The Furusiyya has ended, and I made a name for myself, though not the one I hoped for. I lost to every challenger, and when I pushed through the crowd and fled from the last wrestling bout, I could hear the laughter behind me...
The shame of it all!
The Furusiyya has ended, and I have learned much from the skilled warriors who came. My swordsmanship and my archery are both the better for it.
I am better for it.
The Furusiyya has ended, and the moves I had practised did not work against real, thinking opponents. I am not quite the fighter I thought I was...
Perhaps if I improved my footwork...
